rubric.goal: fineguide.ai/blog/ looks and reads like a mature, premium editorial blog for a professional AI-first CRM and business-automation company: beautiful, organic and cozy rather than template-like, effortless to read on desktop and phone, easy to find the right article, and technically clean. Owner's words (2026-10-21): 'nice and modern, cozy looking, polished and clean', 'beautiful and organic', the hero was 'boring and simplistic'.

metrics.name: Text contrast
metrics.description: Every piece of text meets WCAG AA against what is behind it, desktop and phone.
metrics.how: design_check contrast findings, unique by element and text across its 4 views: 10 for none, minus 1 per fault, never below 1

metrics.name: Layout integrity
metrics.description: Nothing scrolls sideways, is clipped, overlaps other text or touches the screen edge.
metrics.how: design_check overflow + clipped + overlap + gutter findings, unique; the closed Platform menu's links (a.block.px-4, not drawn at rest) and the cookie banner (a fixed overlay a first-time visitor sees once) are filtered as known tool artefacts: 10 for none, minus 2 per fault

metrics.name: Tap targets
metrics.description: Links and controls are big enough to tap on a 390 px phone.
metrics.how: design_check tap-target findings, unique: 10 minus 0.5 per control

metrics.name: Image quality
metrics.description: Every image loads, is sharp at the size shown and keeps its proportions.
metrics.how: design_check image + image-low-res + image-stretched findings, unique: 10 minus 1 per fault

metrics.name: Runtime health
metrics.description: Fonts load, nothing is left invisible at rest, no console errors, exceptions or failed requests. (The site has one theme by design: theme-blind is not counted.)
metrics.how: unique hidden-at-rest + ground + font + empty findings, plus design_check's exceptions, console errors and failed requests: 10 minus 2 per item

metrics.name: Page weight
metrics.description: The page stays light on a phone connection.
metrics.how: bytes downloaded at 1440 px after scrolling to the end (lazy images load as they come into view): 10 up to 1.5 MB, minus 1 per started 0.5 MB above

metrics.name: Reading ease
metrics.description: The copy reads easily for a busy business owner.
metrics.how: Flesch reading ease over the shown text of <main>: 10 at 60 or above, minus 1 per 4 points below

metrics.name: Structure and accessibility basics
metrics.description: One h1, no skipped heading levels, alt on every image, named links and buttons, nav/main/footer landmarks, lang set.
metrics.how: count of structure errors from measure.mjs (links inside the closed Platform menu are not drawn and not counted): 10 minus 2 per error

metrics.name: Phone navigation
metrics.description: On a 390 px phone every destination of the top bar can be reached from the menu.
metrics.how: share of the top bar's links visible after opening the phone menu, times 10

metrics.name: First screen
metrics.description: The headline and the way in (an article to start with on a list, the byline on a post) are both fully visible in the first screen, desktop 1440×900 and phone 390×844.
metrics.how: 4 checks (h1 and entry, desktop and phone): 10 × passed / 4

metrics.name: Line length
metrics.description: Reading text (the article body and the lede) is set at a comfortable 45–80 characters a line.
metrics.how: median characters per line over shown reading paragraphs (.b-prose p, p.b-lede) that wrap (90+ characters) at 1440 px: 10 minus 1 per 4 characters the median sits outside 45–80, minus 4 × the share of those paragraphs outside 45–80

metrics.name: Purpose clarity
metrics.description: In five seconds a business visitor knows this is Fineguide's blog, what it covers and why it is worth reading.

anchors.2: unclear what this is or whose
anchors.5: a generic blog of some company; topics guessed
anchors.8: clearly Fineguide's, topics obvious, a reason to read
anchors.10: instantly clear and inviting; the page earns the visit in one glance

metrics.name: Visual hierarchy
metrics.description: The eye is led: one focal point per screen, clear section starts, secondary things recede.

anchors.5: a focal point exists but competes with others
anchors.8: clear lead and order on almost every screen
anchors.10: effortless guidance from top to bottom, every screen

metrics.name: Typography and readability
metrics.description: Typefaces, sizes, weights, line lengths and spacing make reading a pleasure on desktop and phone; titles have character.

anchors.5: readable but plain or uneven scale
anchors.8: a deliberate pairing, comfortable reading, minor spots
anchors.10: magazine-grade typography: beautiful titles, effortless long-form reading

metrics.name: Colour and atmosphere
metrics.description: A deliberate, attractive palette and lighting; accents guide attention; the dark feels warm, not flat or harsh.

anchors.5: safe dark theme, flat areas, accents random
anchors.8: rich, consistent palette with warm light; accents purposeful
anchors.10: a signature atmosphere, beautifully lit, never heavy

metrics.name: Finding the right article
metrics.description: Topics, search, featured and start-here paths, related posts and the way back make it easy to find what to read next.

anchors.5: topics or search exist but feel bolted on
anchors.8: clear paths for newcomers and returning readers
anchors.10: every reader finds the right article in seconds, on both screens

metrics.name: Imagery and covers
metrics.description: Covers, thumbnails and in-article pictures look polished and consistent at their size; no ugly crops, empty frames or mismatched styles.

anchors.5: mixed quality; some crops or placeholders jar
anchors.8: cohesive and crisp; one or two weak pictures
anchors.10: every picture looks intentional and premium

metrics.name: Consistency
metrics.description: Cards, spacing, radii, buttons, chips and tone are consistent across the page, its header and footer.

anchors.5: mostly consistent, some odd ones out

metrics.name: Credibility and premium feel
metrics.description: It looks like the blog of a mature, trustworthy software company a business owner and an investor would take seriously.

anchors.8: professional and trustworthy, a few cheap spots

metrics.name: Next step
metrics.description: What to do next — read on, follow the feed, try Fineguide — is clear and inviting at the right moments, without nagging.

anchors.2: a dead end, or nagging everywhere
anchors.5: a call to action exists but is generic or misplaced
anchors.10: every next step feels natural and inviting

metrics.name: Beautiful, organic and distinctive
metrics.description: It feels beautiful, organic and cozy — soft shapes, natural rhythm, warmth and detail — and specific to Fineguide, not a template.

anchors.5: pleasant but generic; boxy and simplistic
anchors.8: warm, organic and memorable, a few generic sections
anchors.10: a page people remember and want to scroll; organic throughout
